## Overview

NICHESv2 computes ligand-receptor-mediated (LRM) signaling scores between pairs of cells
in single-cell or spatial transcriptomic data. For each pair of cells and each valid
ligand-receptor pair in your database, it asks: does the sending cell express the ligand,
and does the receiving cell express the receptor? If so, it records a score for that
communication event.

The result is stored in a **NICHESObject** — a custom S3 object designed for this specific
kind of data. Before diving into a full analysis workflow, this vignette walks through the
structure of a NICHESObject so that you know exactly what you are working with and how to
access it.

NICHESv2 ships with two bundled datasets:

- `NICHESv2_inputs` — the raw ingredients: a count matrix, cell metadata, and an LR
  database. This is what you pass into `create_NICHESObject()`.
- `NICHESv2_example` — a pre-built NICHESObject (80 cells, spatial mode, 15 LR pairs)
  ready to explore.

```{r load-package}
library(NICHESv2)
library(data.table)
```

---

## The raw inputs

Load the bundled inputs to see what `create_NICHESObject()` expects.

```{r load-inputs}
data(NICHESv2_inputs)
names(NICHESv2_inputs)
```

### Count matrix

```{r count-matrix}
dim(NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx)
NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx[1:4, 1:4]
```

Rows are genes, columns are cell barcodes. The matrix is sparse (`dgCMatrix`). Genes
are human gene symbols; barcodes are the same identifiers used in the metadata.

### Cell metadata

```{r meta-data}
head(NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data, n = 4)
```

Each row is one cell. At minimum, metadata must contain spatial coordinates (`x`, `y`)
for spatial mode, or cell-type annotations for sampled mode and pseudobulk analysis.
Additional columns (sample ID, condition, cluster label) can be carried through and will
appear on every edge in the final object.

### LR database

```{r lr-db}
head(NICHESv2_inputs$LRM.db, n = 6)
nrow(NICHESv2_inputs$LRM.db)
```

Each row is one ligand-receptor pair. The two required columns are `ligand` and
`receptor`, containing gene symbols (or underscore-delimited complexes such as
`COL1A1_COL1A2`). NICHESv2 ships with FANTOM5 databases for human, mouse, rat, and
pig; you can also supply your own data frame or use OmniPath via `load_LRM_database()`.

---

## The NICHESObject

Load the pre-built example and print a summary.

```{r load-example}
data(NICHESv2_example)
print(NICHESv2_example)
```

The print summary shows the four key quantities at a glance: how many cells, how many
genes, how many edges (cell pairs), and how many valid LRM pairs were scored.

A NICHESObject is a named list with 14 slots, accessed with `$` exactly as you would
any R list.

```{r slot-names}
names(NICHESv2_example)
```

The slots fall into four groups: **cell**, **edge**, **neighborhood**, and
**gene / LRM**. We cover each below.

---

## Cell slots

### `$cell.list` — all barcodes

```{r cell-list}
length(NICHESv2_example$cell.list)
head(NICHESv2_example$cell.list)
```

A character vector of all cell barcodes in the object. This is the canonical identifier
used throughout — every other slot references barcodes by this string.

### `$cell.data` — per-cell expression (sparse, long format)

```{r cell-data}
NICHESv2_example$cell.data
```

This is a `data.table` in **long format**: one row per (cell, gene) combination where
expression is non-zero. Columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cell` | Cell barcode |
| `gene` | Gene symbol |
| `score` | Raw count value |
| `score.norm` | Proportional expression within this cell (count / cell total) |

Because the table is sparse, genes with zero expression in a given cell simply have no
row. This keeps memory use manageable even for large datasets.

The table is keyed on `(cell, gene)`, so lookups by cell or gene are fast:

```{r cell-data-query}
# Expression profile of a single cell
NICHESv2_example$cell.data[cell == NICHESv2_example$cell.list[1]]
```

### `$cell.meta` — cell-level metadata

```{r cell-meta}
head(NICHESv2_example$cell.meta)
```

One row per cell. Always contains `cell` (barcode), `x`, and `y` (spatial coordinates
in spatial mode). Additional columns from the metadata supplied at construction time are
carried through here.

---

## Edge slots

An **edge** is a directed cell pair: one sending cell and one receiving cell. The edge
ID is `"SendingCell|ReceivingCell"` — a pipe-delimited string that uniquely identifies
the pair.

### `$edge.list` — index of all edges

```{r edge-list}
head(NICHESv2_example$edge.list)
nrow(NICHESv2_example$edge.list)
```

Three columns: `edge` (the ID string), `SendingCell`, `ReceivingCell`. This is the
master index — all other edge slots reference edges by the `edge` ID.

### `$edge.data` — LRM scores (sparse, long format)

```{r edge-data}
NICHESv2_example$edge.data
```

One row per (edge, LRM) combination with a non-zero score. Columns:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `edge` | Edge ID (`"SendingCell\|ReceivingCell"`) |
| `LRM` | LR pair ID (`"ligand\|receptor"`) |
| `score` | Raw signaling score (product or minimum of expression values) |
| `score.norm` | Score as a proportion of all LRM scores on this edge |

Again sparse: if neither cell expresses a given ligand-receptor pair, there is no row.

```{r edge-data-query}
# Top LRM pairs by mean score across all edges
top.lrms <- NICHESv2_example$edge.data[
  , .(mean.score = mean(score)), by = LRM
][order(-mean.score)]
head(top.lrms, n = 8)
```

### `$edge.meta` — edge-level metadata

```{r edge-meta}
head(NICHESv2_example$edge.meta, n = 3)
```

One row per edge. Contains `edge`, `SendingCell`, `ReceivingCell`, then all cell-level
metadata columns duplicated with `Sending.` and `Receiving.` prefixes. Character/factor
columns shared between sender and receiver are also summarised as `Joint.*` columns.
This slot is what you use for filtering edges by cell type, condition, or spatial region.

```{r edge-meta-query}
# How many edges per sending cell type?
NICHESv2_example$edge.meta[, .N, by = Sending.celltype][order(-N)]
```

---

## Neighborhood slots

```{r neighborhood-slots}
NICHESv2_example$neighborhood.cell.list
```

The three neighborhood slots (`$neighborhood.cell.list`, `$neighborhood.edge.list`,
`$neighborhood.meta`) are `NULL` by default. They are populated when you call
`add_neighborhoods()`. They store, for each cell, the list of neighboring cells and
edges that fall within its defined spatial neighborhood. See the spatial vignette for
a worked example.

---

## Gene and LRM slots

### `$gene.list` and `$gene.meta`

```{r gene-slots}
length(NICHESv2_example$gene.list)
head(NICHESv2_example$gene.list)
```

`$gene.list` is the full set of genes from the original count matrix. `$gene.meta`
holds any per-gene annotations you supplied; it is `NULL` if none were provided.

### `$LRM.list` and `$LRM.meta`

```{r lrm-slots}
NICHESv2_example$LRM.list
head(NICHESv2_example$LRM.meta)
```

`$LRM.list` contains only LRM pairs that passed filtering — i.e., both ligand and
receptor were present in the count matrix and expressed in at least one cell.
`$LRM.meta` carries the full annotation from the LR database for these pairs.

---

## Object attributes

Two attributes are attached to every NICHESObject and record how it was constructed:

```{r attributes}
attr(NICHESv2_example, "mode")        # "spatial" or "sampled"
attr(NICHESv2_example, "sample.col")  # NULL if no sample splitting was used
```

These are used internally by several functions and are preserved when objects are
merged with `merge_NICHESObjects()`.

---

## A note on the data structure

If you are used to working with Seurat objects or AnnData, the long-format sparse
tables in NICHESv2 may feel unfamiliar. The key reason for this design is **scale**:
for a spatial dataset with 5,000 cells and 100 LRM pairs, the full edge-by-LRM matrix
would have up to 25 million rows — the vast majority of which are zero. Storing only
non-zero scores in a keyed `data.table` keeps the object in memory and fast to query
regardless of dataset size.

The `data.table` package handles all lookups and aggregations. If you are not familiar
with `data.table` syntax, the most useful operations for NICHESv2 are:

```r
# Filter rows
dt[column == value]

# Compute group summaries
dt[, .(mean.score = mean(score)), by = LRM]

# Subset to specific cells or edges
dt[cell %in% my.cells]
```
